items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: Bill Moore was a beautiful trumpet player. He joined me during the war days.

ctx.x: Ace Harris followed him. I just took Ace Harris up to my apartment and played a record of "After Hours". I said if you play piano good, you've got to play "After Hours" because
that's one of the first tunes that people ask for in the theater.
So, that tune wasn't down on paper cause that was taken from the head of Avery Parrish. So, he played it, and he played it more like Avery than anybody I've heard play it.
